events.excerpt: You can’t expect ATOM’s price to rise significantly while inflation continues to dilute holders and new tokens keep entering the market. Lower inflation. Fewer new tokens. A well-designed burn mechanism. Stronger real demand. These are the changes Cosmos needs to restore confidence in ATOM. Technical upgrades are important, but if they don’t translate into real demand for ATOM, what is the point? Holding ATOM must become genuinely attractive. The token needs stronger utility, and the growth of the Cosmos ecosystem must finally translate into value for ATOM holders. Cosmos has the potential, but potential alone is not enough. We need concrete decisions and measurable results. Without meaningful tokenomics reform and sustainable demand, ATOM risks continuing to underperform, even if the ecosystem keeps growing. It’s time to stop making promises and start delivering results. ATOM deserves better. 5 posts - 4 participants Read full topic

events.excerpt: Two threads here this month made me look at the same problem from both ends. In one , a holder has ATOM on UX Chain, which halted in July, and RoboMcGobo explained why the Hub can’t just release it: the escrow only opens when the other chain burns the voucher, and that chain makes no blocks. In the other, Akash’s proposal 346 (voting until 2 November) starts a migration that ends with akashnet-2 halting 90 days after a later cutover. So I went through ibc-go (v10.7.0, the version Gaia v29.0.1 runs; akashnet-2 runs v10.5.0, and the transfer code I cite is the same there) to list what has to happen before the last block, because after it nobody can fix anything from the other side. This is not about whether any chain should leave. It’s only about the tokens. Why tokens get stuck When a token leaves its home chain, it goes into that chain’s escrow for the channel and the other side mints a voucher. The escrow releases it only when a packet shows the voucher was burned, and that packet has to come from a live chain. Transfer channels can’t be closed. The transfer module rejects ChanCloseInit , so there is no close-and-settle step. Every packet, ack and timeout is checked through the counterparty’s light client, and the client has to be Active. events.headline: What has to happen to IBC tokens before a Cosmos chain halts for good

events.excerpt: CODE_COLOR: CODE_YELLOW_MAINNET RELEASE_VERSION: 2.14.0 PROTOCOL_UPGRADE: TRUE DATABASE_UPGRADE: TRUE SECURITY_UPGRADE: FALSE Protocol Changes Remove gas rewards: executing a FunctionCall no longer pays part of the burned gas back to the contract account as a reward. The burnt_gas_reward parameter is changed from 30% (3/10) to 0%. See HSP-027 Added an ml_dsa_verify host function so contracts can verify FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signatures on-chain. It takes the signature (3309 bytes), an arbitrary-length message, and the raw 1952-byte public key, each passed either from memory or from a register, and returns 1 for a valid signature or 0 for an invalid one; a wrongly-sized signature or public key aborts the call with MlDsaVerifyInvalidInput . The message is verified as-is with an empty context string, so callers must not pre-hash it. It costs a fixed base cost of 540 Ggas and a dynamic per-byte cost of 11 Mgas per byte. The per-receipt storage proof limit now applies to every action in a receipt, not just FunctionCall . The recorded proof is checked after each action, and a receipt that goes over per_receipt_storage_proof_size_limit (4 MB) fails at that action with the new ReceiptStorageProofSizeExceeded error; the actions after it do not run. events.excerpt: Russia's central bank is rapidly widening the list of firms allowed to trade crypto, as the country's two biggest lenders prepare to sell Bitcoin and other coins to ordinary customers before the end of the year. The Bank of Russia added a 17th company, Prosto LLC, to its register of crypto exchange providers on Thursday, according to a notice on the regulator's website . The register had four members when it opened on 6 October. The separate register of digital depositories, which record who owns which coins, now has eight. The registrations put into practice a law "On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights", which took effect on 1 September and brings crypto trading inside Russia's regulated financial system for the first time. Sberbank and VTB hold both licences Sberbank and VTB, Russia's largest state-controlled banks, were among the first five digital depositories approved on 6 October, the central bank said . VTB was also listed as a crypto exchange provider that day. Sberbank joined the exchange register on 12 October, Interfax reported . events.excerpt: Hi everyone, We just opened the public testnet of Luggom, a Cosmos SDK app-chain with one job: turn a real tax payment into money you own, proven end to end with TLSNotary. No KYC. No third parties. The bank session never leaves the user's device. ## Why another chain? Because Cosmos is at its best when an app-chain brings a new kind of user. Luggom brings the taxpayer. There is no subsidy and no token sale. The inflow is a real payment that already leaves people's accounts every year. The chain's job is to prove it happened and mint against it. ## How it works 1. The user pays a real tax at their bank, as always. 2. TLSNotary proves the paid receipt without exposing the session. 3. The notary signs the attestation; the chain verifies it and mints. 4. Each receipt mines exactly once (payment_id + proof_commitment anti-replay). The desktop app (Tauri/Rust) builds the proof request and signs locally. The seed never leaves the device. What is live - chain-id: `luggom-test` - RPC: `https://rpc.luggom.com` - LCD: `https://lcd.luggom.com` - API: `https://api.luggom.com` - Notary: `wss://notary.luggom.com/session` - Full nodes: open (p2p 26656) — seed `1530baa7b3a07e0cab8dc81c9c08fccc51a47471@62.146.183.122:26656` - Validators: by invitation (the operator funds 200 testnet LUG) - App +
events.headline: Luggom — a Cosmos SDK app-chain where you mine LUG by paying real taxes (public testnet)

This proposal introduces a **Dual-Token Mirror Staking Model** designed to be adopted by consumer chains or app-chains. It rewards aligned validators with a premium yield tier funded entirely by taxing unaligned (“Slacker”) validators, creating a systemic, non-inflationary supply shock for ATOM. -– ## The Problem: The ATOM Yield Trap Current app-chain models rely heavily on hyper-inflation to sustain high staking yields. events.excerpt: Hey Cosmonauts, I’ve been exploring an idea for a privacy-focused Cosmos SDK chain and wanted to bring it here before going too far into implementation. The idea is called VeilRoute — a sovereign Cosmos blockchain that acts as a confidential settlement and asset-routing layer between IBC-connected chains. The problem I’m interested in is relatively simple: Cosmos has interoperability through IBC, but what if applications could route assets through a common privacy layer without publicly exposing every internal transfer, amount, balance, or ownership relationship? I’m not proposing changes to the Cosmos Hub or requesting governance funding. This is an early architectural discussion to get technical feedback from people working on Cosmos SDK, IBC, ZK systems, and interchain security. 1. The idea Imagine a user moving ATOM from Cosmos Hub to Osmosis. Today, the public source and destination transactions are observable, along with the relevant IBC packet information. events.excerpt: Should the Cosmos Hub have its own price oracle? CosmWasm is now permissionless on the Hub, but there is no price oracle available to contracts. Pyth dropped CosmWasm, SEDA is EVM-only, and Band over IBC is slow and costs fees on every query. Without prices, we can’t build any advanced defi on the Hub. So these apps get built on chains like Injective or dYdX, and ATOM ends up used everywhere except on its own chain. Idea: integrate an enshrined oracle based on the Slinky fork. Validators would publish prices at every block, secured by the Hub’s own validator set, with no dependency on an external provider. And beyond the Hub: these prices could be distributed over IBC to any connected chain that lacks an oracle. The Hub would become an interchain’s price provider, with fees flowing back to ATOM stakers. Longer term: prices are only the first step. The same validator-voted mechanism could later carry other data the interchain needs, such as LST exchange rates, proof of reserves or other verified off-chain data. The Hub would become the interchain’s trusted data layer. The Community Pool could fund the development and audit. Would you support this direction? Validators, would you be willing to run an oracle sidecar? 20 posts - 7 participants Read full topic
events.headline: Oracle on Cosmos Hub
